title.en: Rivers of the world and their mouths

description.en: 50 major rivers of the world and the water each one flows into: a sea, ocean, bay, lake or another river. The rivers come from every continent except Antarctica, seven of them Nordic, such as the Torne and the Göta älv. Front: the river; back: where it flows into, in English and Swedish. The mouth is a water that Wikidata records for the river (P403); where it records several, the card gives the sea or bay that the other sources also name, sometimes with a note. Rivers whose mouth is disputed or splits between different waters are left out. From Wikidata, checked against Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin.
description.sv: 50 av världens stora floder och det vatten som var och en mynnar i: ett hav, en ocean, en vik, en sjö eller en annan flod. Floderna kommer från alla världsdelar utom Antarktis, sju av dem nordiska, som Torne älv och Göta älv. Framsida: floden; baksida: var den mynnar, på engelska och svenska. Mynningen är ett vatten som Wikidata anger för floden (P403, mynnar i); där Wikidata anger flera ger kortet det hav eller den vik som även de andra källorna nämner, ibland med en anteckning. Floder vars mynning är omstridd eller delas mellan olika vatten är utelämnade. Uppgifterna kommer från Wikidata och är kontrollerade mot Wikipedia och Nationalencyklopedin.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Candidates (query 1): a list of 99 rivers, written by the compiler to cover every continent and the Nordic countries and including well-known tributaries, was looked up in Wikidata by the titles of their English Wikipedia articles, with every P403 (mouth of the watercourse) statement, its rank and the English and Swedish labels of river and mouth. Rivers whose English article title did not match (the Torne, Ob, Yenisei, Lena, St. Lawrence, Ångermanälven, Tana and Kymijoki) were looked up by their Swedish article titles (query 2). The Lena has no P403 statement and was dropped.

2. Selection: from the candidates the compiler chose 50 rivers whose mouth is one named water that every source checked agrees on (see Selection). For each, query 4 fetched every P403 statement with its rank, and query 3 every English, Swedish and multilingual (mul) label and alias of the rivers and of the waters they flow into. Query 6 fetched P361 (part of), P403, P200 (inflows) and P31 (instance of) of some of the waters, for the notes; query 7 checked whether any Wikidata item records the Gulf of Ob as the Ob's mouth (none does).

3. The back of each card is the value of the river's P403 statement. Where Wikidata gives more than one value (Elbe: North Sea, German Bight, Heligoland Bight; Loire: Bay of Biscay, Loire estuary; Yenisei: Kara Sea, Yenisei Gulf; Volga: Caspian Sea, Kama), the card names the one item that is a sea, ocean, bay or lake in its own right and that the other sources also name, and a note may name a narrower water (Elbe: German Bight; Yenisei: Yenisei Gulf) or the wider one (Loire: Atlantic Ocean); the Volga card has no note. The Volga's second value, the Kama, is its tributary, not its mouth (see quality control).

4. Names: the English front is the river's short English name ("Danube", "Amazon", "Mississippi"); "River" is kept only where it is part of the name ("Yellow River", "Orange River"), and the Nordic rivers keep their own names as English does ("Göta älv", "Kemijoki"). The English back is the Wikidata English label of the water, except "Gulf of St. Lawrence" (an English alias, matching the front "St. Lawrence"), "Mississippi" and "Murray" (short forms, matching the fronts). The Swedish front and back are the Wikidata Swedish label, or, where Swedish reference works use another established form, a Swedish alias: Darlingfloden (the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article and NE's headword; the Swedish label is "Darling"), Murrayfloden (the form NE uses in its article on the Darling, matching "Darlingfloden" on the same card; the Swedish label is "Murray") and Bohaihavet (the form in the text of the Swedish Wikipedia article on the Yellow River; the Swedish label is "Bohai"). Every Swedish name was compared with the title of the river's Swedish Wikipedia article and with NE's headword or alternative names. NE's headwords for the Yangtze and the Yellow River are "Chang Jiang" and "Huang He" (NE gives "Gula floden" as another name); the cards use the Swedish Wikipedia's and Wikidata's "Yangtze" and "Gula floden" and give the Chinese names in a note. "Saint Lawrencefloden" and "Saint Lawrenceviken" follow the Wikidata Swedish labels, the Swedish Wikipedia and NE, not the hyphenated alias "Saint Lawrence-floden". The notes' Swedish water names are Wikidata Swedish labels, except "Jenisejviken" (Yenisei Gulf), which has no Swedish label or alias in Wikidata and was taken from the Swedish Wikipedia article "Jenisej" (infobox and text).

5. Wikipedia check: the current English and Swedish Wikipedia article of every river (titles from the Wikidata sitelinks, query 5) was fetched with its revision id through the MediaWiki API (fetch_wiki.py and fetch_wiki2.py), and the infobox fields mouth, mouth_location and mynning and the sentences of the text that name the mouth were extracted (mouths.py, which replaces templates such as unit conversions with "…" and removes link markup and references). The card table <scratch>/cards.py holds, for each card, only values that appear in the dossier: the Wikidata items of river and mouth, the names on the card, the notes, the Wikipedia article keys, the NE address and the marker string that picks the quoted sentence. The script make_cards.py (query 14) then wrote the evidence of every card from these extracts and from the saved Wikidata results; the compiler chose for each article the sentence to quote and read every card's evidence against the article.

6. NE check: the article of each river on Nationalencyklopedin (ne.se) was fetched (fetch_ne.py) and the opening shown to visitors without a subscription was read. Article addresses were guessed from the Swedish names; where that failed (Po, Kongo, Niger) a web search on ne.se found the address form "kongo-(flod-afrika)". No NE article was found for the Paraná or the São Francisco, whose cards rest on Wikidata and the two Wikipedias. Britannica was tried first and answered 403 to the research environment: curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -L -o <scratch>/brit-danube.html -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{size_download}\n" https://www.britannica.com/place/Danube-River; it was not used.

7. Mississippi note: the text of Executive Order 14172 was downloaded from the Government Publishing Office (govinfo.gov) and its Sec. 4 read; the note states only what the order did in January 2025, not the name's later use.

8. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata that the river has the P403 value on the back, and that the English and Swedish names on the card are labels or aliases of the river and of the water in that language or in Wikidata's multilingual (mul) set, where they are ("Torne" and "Congo" are mul labels and "Mississippi" a mul alias, not English ones; no English or mul label or alias matches the short English names Mekong, Irrawaddy, Columbia, Mackenzie, Amazon, Paraná, Magdalena, Darling and Murray, which have no label check). make_dossier.py assembled this dossier from cards.json and the text written for it. The notes rest on the Wikidata statements and the order named in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
selection: 50 rivers: 13 in the rest of Europe (Danube, Rhine, Volga, Don, Elbe, Thames, Seine, Loire, Rhône, Po, Tagus, Tiber, and the Ural, conventionally counted as the Europe–Asia boundary along much of its lower course), 7 Nordic (Göta älv, Klarälven, Torne, Kemijoki, Oulujoki, Vuoksi, Kymijoki), 9 in Asia, 8 in Africa, 7 in North America, 5 in South America and 1 in Australia, chosen by the compiler among the world's best-known rivers, with a few well-known tributaries (Blue and White Nile, Missouri, Darling) and rivers flowing into lakes (Klarälven, Vuoksi, Niagara, Jordan). The mouth is a water named by the river's P403 statement in Wikidata (the Loire into the Bay of Biscay, the Torne into the Bothnian Bay, not the Atlantic or the Gulf of Bothnia). Where Wikidata names several waters (the Elbe, Loire and Yenisei), the card gives the sea or bay that the other sources also name (the North Sea, the Bay of Biscay, the Kara Sea) and the note names the narrower or wider water; a river that joins another flows into that river. Left out because sources name different waters as the mouth or the river ends in several: the Ob (Wikidata: Kara Sea; Wikipedia and NE: the Gulf of Ob), Dalälven (Wikidata: Gävle Bay; Swedish Wikipedia: the Bothnian Sea; English Wikipedia: the Gulf of Bothnia), the Glomma (Wikidata and the Wikipedia infoboxes: Skagerrak; the texts: the Oslofjord), the Vistula (a delta into Gdańsk Bay and the Vistula Lagoon), the Oder (Wikidata: Baltic Sea and Szczecin Lagoon), the Dnieper and Dniester (estuaries ranked above or instead of the Black Sea) and the Kama (Wikidata: the Volga, the Kuybyshev Reservoir and the Chusovaya). Left out because Wikidata names no mouth: the Lena. Left out because their Wikidata mouth is a little-known local water (Lule älv, Ume älv, Indalsälven, Kalix älv, Motala ström, the Neva, the Northern Dvina, the Hudson, the Pechora). Left out to keep the deck at about 50 and avoid repeating the same back: the Amur, Brahmaputra, Kolyma, Yalu, Tigris, Amu Darya, Syr Darya, Murray, Colorado, Rio Grande, Ohio, Uruguay, Senegal, Douro, Guadalquivir, Weser, Main, Moselle, Inn, Daugava, Pite älv and others among the 99 candidates. Several big rivers end in a delta (Danube, Nile, Mekong, Ganges, Niger), but into one water, and are included. The Rhine's distributary IJssel flows into the IJsselmeer, but every source checked names the North Sea as the Rhine's mouth.

"""Fetch the current wikitext and revision id of every river's English and Swedish
Wikipedia article (titles from q5.csv) through the MediaWiki API; write wiki.json."""
import csv, json, os, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
titles = {}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(f"{D}/q5.csv", encoding="utf-8")):
    lang = "en" if "en.wikipedia" in r["wiki"] else "sv"
    titles.setdefault(lang, {})[r["title"]] = r["item"].rsplit("/", 1)[1]
out = {}
for lang, ts in titles.items():
    names = sorted(ts)
    for i in range(0, len(names), 25):
        chunk = names[i:i + 25]
        url = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2"
               "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote("|".join(chunk)))
        # one revision per page is only allowed for a single title, so fetch one by one
        for t in chunk:
            u = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2"
                 "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote(t))
            req = urllib.request.Request(u, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
                page = json.load(resp)["query"]["pages"][0]
            rev = page["revisions"][0]
            out[f"{lang}:{t}"] = {"qid": ts[t], "lang": lang, "title": t, "revid": rev["revid"],
                                  "text": rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]}
            time.sleep(0.3)
json.dump(out, open(f"{D}/wiki.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False)
print(len(out), "articles")

# fetch_wiki2.py
"""Add the Irrawaddy and Oulujoki articles (en and sv) to wiki.json, then rerun mouths.py."""
import json, os, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
want = [("en", "Irrawaddy River", "Q26076"), ("sv", "Irrawaddy", "Q26076"),
        ("en", "Oulujoki", "Q736575"), ("sv", "Ule älv", "Q736575")]
out = json.load(open(f"{D}/wiki.json", encoding="utf-8"))
for lang, t, q in want:
    u = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2&redirects=1"
         "&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote(t))
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(u, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60) as resp:
        page = json.load(resp)["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page["revisions"][0]
    out[f"{lang}:{page['title']}"] = {"qid": q, "lang": lang, "title": page["title"], "revid": rev["revid"],
                                      "text": rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]}
    print(lang, page["title"], rev["revid"])
json.dump(out, open(f"{D}/wiki.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False)

# mouths.py
"""Pull the infobox mouth fields and the first lead sentences naming the mouth out of wiki.json."""
import json, os, re
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
w = json.load(open(f"{D}/wiki.json", encoding="utf-8"))
FIELD = re.compile(r"^\s*\|\s*(mouth|mouth_location|mynning|mynningsort|mouth_name|mynning_namn|utlopp|river_mouth)\s*=\s*(.*)$", re.M | re.I)
SENT = re.compile(r"[^.\n]*\b(into|empties|discharges|mynnar|utmynnar|rinner ut|flows into|ut i|mouth|drains)\b[^.\n]*\.", re.I)
def clean(s):
    s = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*/>", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"<ref[^>]*>.*?</ref>", "", s, flags=re.S)
    s = re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'{2,}", "", s)
    return s.strip()
res = {}
for key, a in sorted(w.items(), key=lambda kv: (kv[1]["qid"], kv[0])):
    t = a["text"]
    fields = [(m.group(1), clean(m.group(2))) for m in FIELD.finditer(t)]
    body = re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", re.sub(r"\{\{[^{}]*\}\}", "…", t))
    lead = clean(body)[:6000]
    sents = [clean(m.group(0)) for m in SENT.finditer(lead)][:3]
    res[key] = {"qid": a["qid"], "revid": a["revid"], "fields": fields, "sentences": sents}
    print(f"{a['qid']} {key} rev {a['revid']}")
    for f in fields:
        print("   F", f)
    for s in sents:
        print("   S", s[:300])
json.dump(res, open(f"{D}/mouths.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

"""Fetch the Nationalencyklopedin (ne.se) article of each river and print its headword,
definition and the first part of the text (the part shown to visitors). Saves ne/<slug>.html
and ne.json. Usage: python3 fetch_ne.py slug1 slug2 ..."""
import html, json, os, re, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
os.makedirs(f"{D}/ne", exist_ok=True)
try:
    store = json.load(open(f"{D}/ne.json", encoding="utf-8"))
except FileNotFoundError:
    store = {}
ARGS = sys.argv[1:]
if ARGS and ARGS[0] == "-f":
    ARGS = open(ARGS[1], encoding="utf-8").read().split()
for slug in ARGS:
    url = "https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/" + urllib.parse.quote(slug)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            t = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
            code = resp.status
    except Exception as e:  # noqa
        print(slug, "ERROR", e)
        continue
    open(f"{D}/ne/{slug}.html", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(t)
    canon = re.findall(r'<link rel="canonical" href="([^"]+)"', t)
    i = t.find('<span class="huvud">')
    seg = t[i:i + 6000] if i >= 0 else ""
    seg = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", seg)
    seg = html.unescape(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", seg)).strip()[:900]
    store[slug] = {"url": url, "status": code, "canonical": canon[-1] if canon else "", "text": seg}
    print(f"== {slug} {code} {canon[-1] if canon else ''}\n   {seg}")
    time.sleep(0.5)
json.dump(store, open(f"{D}/ne.json", "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

The choice of 50 rivers is the compiler's own, not taken from any list.
